---
title: "Our Story"
---

ÇAHSPAR grew from a collaboration among nine academics who have spent around 20 years researching, debating and learning together across universities in labour economics, industrial relations and social policy.

Their experience of books, articles, research and projects brought a shared question into focus: how can scholarly knowledge about working life and social policy travel more effectively across institutional and national boundaries, while remaining attentive to the lives and places it seeks to understand?

## From Shared Experience to an International Mission

The association gives institutional form to an ambition to connect researchers, strengthen joint inquiry and make knowledge more accessible. Founded in Türkiye, ÇAHSPAR looks towards a worldwide community of scholars and practitioners concerned with dignified work, social protection and social justice.

Türkiye’s academic experience is a starting point for reciprocal international exchange. We seek to bring research from Türkiye into global debates and to learn from the concepts, methods and experiences developed in other societies.

## Building a Community Across Borders

Our next stage is to develop international research partnerships, comparative projects, joint publications and spaces for sustained academic dialogue. We aim to bring together experienced academics, early-career researchers and doctoral students across disciplines and regions.

Our global research horizon encompasses the 193 UN Member States, with the ILO’s five broad regions providing a reference for comparative work. This ambition will take shape through specific studies and partnerships with clearly stated geographical coverage.

We envisage an association where collaboration continues beyond individual events: researchers can develop questions together, share methodological expertise, challenge assumptions and connect findings with policy and practice.

**Our shared purpose is to build lasting international cooperation in working life and social policy, with scientific quality and public benefit at its centre.**
